analysis.cluster: Armour, matchups and the vocabulary gaps
analysis.summary: Armour class and armour models agreed 100%, but the coders got there unsure. 8 of 12 reports hesitated on armour.class and all 12 on armour.models. The class list gives only example kinds, with no order for which source decides (the game's own word, the kind of unit, or toughness within the game). Three model descriptions contradict their own examples: flat-pool's RA3 example, zonal's Battlefield 4 example and crew-casualties' Company of Heroes example. Three set no threshold: directional, damage-reduction and evasive. I propose: an ordered coding rule for armour classes, anchored on each game's main battle tank; descriptions that name each kind of unit once; coding rules for six armour models; a rule that cover, veterancy and retreat bonuses are not models; and a rule on which titles of a series count. Matchup lists stay open choices. To make them more useful I propose a negated link (!hits:low-air), so a missing ability can be a weakness, and a short guide to choosing links. Of the 102 gaps, five are worth adding before the freeze (negated links, the retreat-to-base and fortify-point patterns, a pay-per-use resource, a thermal sensor trait). About twenty are covered by sharper wording or a field rule in other groups' lists. The rest should wait for the research run's gap report, which needs every gap written into fit_notes with '/' paths.

proposals.evidence: Agreement 100% on all six units (Terror Drone light, Hammer heavy, Multigunner IFV light, Siege Tank heavy, Riflemen unarmoured, attack helicopter light; the RA3 samples agree), but 10 hesitations in 8 of 12 reports (A-ra3 x2, B-ra3, C-ra3 x2, A-sc2, B-sc2, C-sc2, B-coh1, C-battlefield) and 6 unclear-rule notes (A-ra3, A-sc2, B-sc2, C-battlefield, C-ra3, C-sc2). Drone light vs unarmoured (A, B, C: 'light lists drones, but it has half a Conscript's health and an infantry-like armour set'). IFV light vs medium (A, C: the game says Light, but the list names IFVs under medium). Siege Tank heavy vs medium (A, B, C: 'main battle tank' against middling health; no rule says whether the class is relative or absolute; the SC2 hint covers only Massive and Light Biological). Riflemen unarmoured vs light (B: does CoH's basic infantry type count as a 'tougher category'?). Helicopter light vs medium (C: no armour_map, and it is armoured against small arms).
proposals.root_cause: armour-classes describes each class only by example kinds ('IFVs' under medium; 'drones' and 'helicopters' under light; 'main battle tanks' under heavy). The list says only 'how tough the unit is, as a band'. Nothing says whether the game's own label, the kind of unit or its toughness within its game decides, or which wins when they disagree. ra3, sc2, coh1 and battlefield have no armour_map, so the examples were all the coders had. Under light, 'unless their game gives them a tougher category' does not say what counts as a category.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-classes.json: list description and a new tie_breaks array (two entries)
proposals.change:
1) List description, old -> new: 'How tough the unit is, as a band. Combined with one or two armour models on the card.' -> 'How tough the unit is next to the other units of its own game, as a band. Where the game has no armour map, its main battle tank is the fixed point: it is heavy. Combined with one or two armour models on the card.'
2) tie_breaks[0], terms [unarmoured, light, medium, heavy, super-heavy], rule: 'Go through these steps in order and stop at the first one that gives an answer. 1. The game's armour_map in data/games.json, with any step up or down its registry notes name. 2. The game's own armour word for this unit, when the word is light, medium or heavy. Skip this step for Tiberian Dawn, Tiberian Sun, Tiberium Wars, Company of Heroes 1 to 3 and StarCraft II, whose words cut across our classes. 3. The tank named in the game's cost anchor is heavy; in a game without costs, its standard main battle tank. 4. The kinds named in the class descriptions. 5. For a kind named nowhere, compare its health and the weapons that hurt it with that tank (heavy) and with the game's basic rifle infantry (unarmoured). Say in armour.notes which step decided.'
3) tie_breaks[1], terms [unarmoured, light], rule: 'A machine is never unarmoured: a drone or robot with very little health is light. A soldier or animal is unarmoured unless step 1 or 2 lifts it. Protection every soldier of the game can get, such as cover, veterancy ranks or the retreat bonus, never lifts the class; mention it in armour.notes.'
proposals.expected: Terror Drone: no map; its armour set has no class word; not a tank; step 4 'drones' -> light, and tie-break 2 rules out unarmoured (A, B, C and the sample: light). Hammer: step 3, ra3's cost anchor names it -> heavy. Multigunner IFV: step 2, the infobox word 'Light' -> light; the IFV example under medium no longer competes (A, B, C, sample: light). Siege Tank: step 2 skipped for StarCraft II; step 3, sc2's cost anchor is the Siege Tank -> heavy (A, B, C). Riflemen: step 2 skipped for Company of Heroes; step 4 soldiers -> unarmoured; cover and veterancy cannot lift it (A, B, C). Attack helicopter: no map; no word from a lead title (see series-titles); step 4 'helicopters (gunships included)' -> light (A, B, C). Toughness felt from play is not a step, so C's 'medium' doubt has nothing to rest on. Each unit is decided by exactly one step, so no two coders are left free to differ.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Goes with armour-class-descriptions (each kind named once) and armour-registry-notes. Validator: the tie_breaks name real terms; nothing else changes. Units in scope: Tiberian Dawn's Nod Light Tank becomes heavy, because the cost anchor names it. That matches Renegade's armour_map, which already counts it as a heavy vehicle. Tiberian Sun's Titan and Tick tank both become heavy (both in the anchor). StarCraft II Armored ground units weaker than the Siege Tank (Roach, Stalker) fall to step 4 or 5 and come out medium; Massive t3 units come out heavy or super-heavy. Games with a map (Foxhole, Iron Harvest, Tempest Rising, Generals and others) are decided at step 1. That is why the description says 'where the game has no armour map': a map that puts the anchor tank elsewhere must not clash with it.

proposals.evidence: Same 8 of 12 reports as armour-class-order. A-ra3 and C-ra3 unclear rules: the examples (IFVs medium, buggies and drones light) conflict with the game's own category. C-sc2: 'main battle tanks' as an example, but no statement that the class is relative to the game.
proposals.root_cause: The descriptions are bare example lists. A kind can sit in two classes (a buggy-like IFV; 'armoured infantry' under light against 'power suits' under medium). No description says what toughness the band means within its game.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-classes.json terms unarmoured, light, medium, heavy, super-heavy: description
proposals.change:
unarmoured: 'Flesh and cloth: soldiers and animals.' -> 'Flesh and cloth: soldiers, animals and creatures without armour plating. A game's basic rifle infantry is unarmoured. Never a machine.'
light: 'Buggies, drones, helicopters and armoured infantry. Soldiers are unarmoured unless their game gives them a tougher category.' -> 'Machines that light weapons still hurt, and soldiers in real armour: buggies, jeeps and trucks, drones, helicopters (gunships included), planes and boats, and soldiers whose game puts them a step above its basic rifle infantry (heavy infantry, power armour).'
medium: 'IFVs, light tanks, power suits, light walkers.' -> 'Shrugs off most light weapons but is clearly weaker than the game's main battle tank: IFVs and APCs, light tanks, exosuits bigger than a soldier, and light walkers.'
heavy: 'Main battle tanks and assault mechs.' -> 'The game's main battle tank and units about as tough: other battle tanks and assault mechs.'
super-heavy: 'Super-heavy tanks, giant mechs and airships.' -> 'Clearly tougher than the game's main battle tank: super-heavy tanks, giant mechs and airships.'
proposals.expected: Step 4 of armour-class-order now gives one answer per kind. Drone -> light; attack helicopter -> light (gunships named); Riflemen -> unarmoured (basic rifle infantry). An IFV is medium only when its game gives no word of its own; RA3's IFV has the word Light, so it stays light. Hammer and Siege Tank -> heavy (the game's main battle tank). A, B and C code all six units as they did, and the hesitations lose their cause.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. No change to allowed maps or ranks. 'Power armour' (a soldier in armour, light) and 'exosuits bigger than a soldier' (medium) are now told apart, which matches the bodies list (power-suit at small size is infantry, at medium a walker). Jets and bombers now have a home (planes, light), so a unit like a heavy bomber reaches medium or heavier only through a map, a game word or step 5.

proposals.evidence: A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 all weighed unarmoured for the Terror Drone because its armour set is infantry-like (3 of 3 reports that coded it).
proposals.root_cause: Nothing stops a machine from being coded or rolled as 'flesh and cloth'.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-classes.json term unarmoured, allowed
proposals.change: allowed: {"sizes": ["tiny", "small"]} -> {"sizes": ["tiny", "small"], "nature": ["organic"]}
proposals.expected: No pilot unit changes: the drone is light, and the only unarmoured unit (Riflemen) is organic. If a coder ever codes a machine as unarmoured, the validator prints an ATYPICAL line, which shows the slip at once.
proposals.side_effects: nature is a list the combination rules read (UNIT_PARTS), so the map is valid. The example card (an uncrewed-machine drone, light) and the samples still pass. The generator will never roll an unarmoured machine. No real unit in scope should break it: RA2's terror drone maps to light, and ARC Raiders machines start at light.

proposals.evidence: A-sc2, B-sc2, C-sc2 and A-ra3, C-ra3 (5 reports) asked for an armour_map for sc2 or ra3, or said the registry hint does not decide. B-sc2: 'The registry hint covers Massive and Light Biological only, not plain Armored.'
proposals.root_cause: games-r1.md says RA3 maps per unit but gives no rule. games-r5.md gives SC2 hints only for Massive and Light Biological units, and says nothing about plain Armored units or the anchor tank.
proposals.target: research/registry-notes/games-r1.md (RA3 'No armour_map suggested' bullet) and research/registry-notes/games-r5.md ('No maps for SupCom, PA, SC2 or HW2' bullet); data/games.json unchanged
proposals.change:
Keep ra3 and sc2 without an armour_map. RA3 gives each unit its own armour set with percentages (BaseTankArmor, BaseHarassmentVehicleArmor and so on), and only a few infoboxes carry a plain word. SC2's attributes cut across our classes: Armored covers both the Siege Tank and the Roach. A map with one class per key would code both wrongly.
games-r1.md, RA3 bullet, append: 'Where an infobox gives a plain armour word (Light, Medium or Heavy), that word decides (step 2 of the armour-class order in the armour-classes list). The three main battle tanks in the cost anchor are heavy. Everything else follows that order.'
games-r5.md, replace 'Use them as hints: Massive means heavy or super-heavy, and Light Biological infantry means unarmoured.' with 'Use them only as hints inside the armour-class order. The Siege Tank, the cost anchor, is heavy. Armored ground vehicles and walkers clearly weaker than it are medium, and armoured infantry such as the Marauder is light. Massive units are heavy, or super-heavy at t3 when clearly tougher than the Siege Tank. Light Biological infantry is unarmoured, and Light machines are light.'
proposals.expected: Siege Tank heavy (A, B, C). Multigunner IFV light from its infobox word (A, B, C). Terror Drone light (its infobox gives an armour set with no word, so steps 4 and 5 decide). Hammer heavy (anchor).
proposals.side_effects: Notes only; no validator change. Units in scope for the research run: SC2 Roach, Stalker and Cyclone come out medium; the Marauder light; the Thor, Ultralisk and Battlecruiser heavy or super-heavy.

proposals.evidence: 8 reports quoted flat-pool's 'used only when no other model applies' against a case where it seemed to apply too: A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 on the Hammer (flat-pool + directional?); A-sc2, B-sc2 and C-sc2 on the Siege Tank; A-coh1 and B-coh1 on the Riflemen. B-ra3: 'its own example describes RA3's per-armour-type scaling', which every RA3 unit has, the directional Hammer included. B-ra3 unclear rule on flat-pool vs directional. All coders and the sample still agreed (Hammer directional alone; drone and IFV flat-pool alone).
proposals.root_cause: flat-pool is both a fallback ('used only when no other model applies') and a definition ('one health bar'), which is true of nearly every unit. Its RA3 example (damage first scaled by the armour type) describes something every RA3 unit has, so the example contradicts the fallback rule. Nothing says whether it may sit next to another model.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json term flat-pool: description, new source_rule, examples[0]
proposals.change:
description: 'One health bar; every hit subtracts. The easiest to read. Used only when no other model applies.' -> 'One health bar and nothing more: every hit just subtracts. The easiest to read.'
source_rule (new): 'Code it only when no other model on this list applies, and never together with another model. Damage scaled by armour type or class, as in most strategy games, is the armour class's job: it does not rule out flat-pool, and it does not make the unit another model.'
examples[0]: 'Red Alert 3: one health value per unit, with damage first scaled by the unit's armour type' -> 'Red Alert 3: the Multigunner IFV has one health value; its armour type only scales the damage each kind of weapon does'
proposals.expected: Hammer: directional alone (A, B, C, sample). Terror Drone and IFV: flat-pool alone (A, B, C, sample). Riflemen: flat-pool alone (A, B, C; see shared-bonuses-not-models). Siege Tank: flat-pool alone (see damage-reduction-threshold). Attack helicopter: critical-burn, self-repair, zonal, no flat-pool. Nobody can add flat-pool next to another model.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Optional: add excluded.armour-models (every other id) to flat-pool, so a card never pairs it with a model. Not recommended: on a researched unit a break would be a coding slip, not an atypical unit. The generator should treat flat-pool as 'no special model' and roll it alone.

proposals.evidence: B-ra3 hesitated on directional for the Terror Drone and the IFV ('only the tank armour sets show it'). A-ra3, B-ra3 and C-ra3 hesitated on how mild a bonus still counts for the Hammer ('side and rear hits add only 5 to 10 percent'). B-ra3 unclear rule: 'Nothing says how small a side or rear bonus still counts as directional.' 3 of 3 ra3 reports.
proposals.root_cause: The directional term gives RA3 as a 'mild' example, but does not say whether the facing values must belong to the unit itself or to the game, or how small a bonus may be.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json term directional: new source_rule; RA3 example
proposals.change:
source_rule (new): 'Code it when the unit's own data, or a rule its game applies to every unit of its kind, makes side or rear hits do more, however little; say how much in armour.notes. Leave it out when neither gives this unit facing values, even if some other units of its game have them.'
example: 'Red Alert 3: mild; side and rear hits do slightly more' -> 'Red Alert 3: mild; the tank armour sets take a little more damage on the sides and rear'
proposals.expected: Hammer: its armour set gives side and rear values -> directional (A, B, C, sample). Terror Drone: its armour set has no facing values -> no directional, flat-pool (B's doubt settled). IFV: the infobox gives only 'Light' -> flat-pool. Company of Heroes vehicles: the game's rear-armour rule covers every vehicle -> directional.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. No validator change. Consistent with shared-bonuses-not-models, which keeps game-wide armour mechanics (CoH rear armour) and drops only bonuses from position or rank.

proposals.evidence: All three SC2 reports hesitated (A-sc2, B-sc2, C-sc2): 'every SC2 unit has flat armour, and the tank's is tiny (1 point)'; 'coded literally, every SC2 unit gets damage-reduction'. All three chose damage-reduction and named flat-pool as the alternative. A-sc2 unclear rule asks for a threshold. C-battlefield: 'if they ignore small arms, damage-reduction would fit, but it is barred on light'. B-ra3 (Hammer): '0 percent from sniper and melee and 50 percent from guns resembles damage reduction, but by percentage'.
proposals.root_cause: The term's StarCraft II example covers any armour value however small, so the term no longer separates units. No rule says that a cut by percentage or by damage type (RA3 armour sets, Battlefield vehicles ignoring bullets) belongs to the armour class and damage map, not to this model. The PlanetSide 2 example ('tanks ignore small arms') is such a damage-type resist, which makes it worse.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json term damage-reduction: new source_rule; examples
proposals.change:
source_rule (new): 'Code it only when the game takes a fixed amount off each hit, and the amount changes which weapons work: the game's basic rifle or light gun loses a large share of each hit to it, about a quarter or more. Judge the unit without faction-wide upgrades. A smaller value only trims hits; mention it in armour.notes. A cut by percentage or by damage type (guns doing half damage to tanks, small arms doing nothing to vehicles) is the armour class and the damage map, not this model.'
examples: replace 'StarCraft II: armour takes a fixed amount off every hit, but every hit still does a little damage' with 'StarCraft II: each unit's armour value comes off every hit; on the most armoured units, such as an Ultralisk with its plating upgrade, rapid light fire does much less'. Remove 'PlanetSide 2: main battle tanks ignore small arms completely' (a resist by damage type).
proposals.expected: Siege Tank: a Marine shot loses well under a quarter to its small armour -> no damage-reduction -> flat-pool (A, B and C move together, to the alternative all three named). Attack helicopter: bullets do nothing because of the damage type, not a flat amount -> no damage-reduction (C's doubt settled). Hammer: percentage cuts -> not damage-reduction (B's doubt settled).
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Armour model agreement on the Siege Tank stays 100% (all move). Also avoids ATYPICAL noise in the research run: SC2 Light units with a point of armour (Zealot, Mutalisk) would otherwise break damage-reduction's allowed.armour-classes. Units that keep it: SC2 Ultralisk, Battlecruiser and other high-armour units. PlanetSide 2 tanks get small-arms immunity from the damage map instead.

proposals.evidence: A-battlefield, B-battlefield and C-battlefield all coded zonal and all hesitated: 'Zonal's definition is about parts that break, but its seen-in list names Battlefield 4 mobility kills, which are triggered by heavy hits anywhere'. Gaps A-battlefield and B-battlefield wanted 'control loss on heavy hits'. A-battlefield unclear rule: 'Coders following the definition and coders following the examples will split.' 3 of 3 battlefield reports.
proposals.root_cause: The description says hits 'land on parts', which reads as location-based. Two of its own examples are not location-based: Battlefield 4 mobility hits come from hit strength, and Company of Heroes criticals come by chance. Definition and examples contradict each other.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json term zonal: description, new source_rule, Battlefield 4 example
proposals.change:
description: 'Hits land on parts such as tracks, turret, engine, legs or a weapon, which can break and switch off functions before the unit dies.' -> 'Parts such as tracks, turret, engine, rotor, legs or a weapon can be knocked out before the unit dies, switching that function off for a while or for good. The part may be chosen by where the hit lands, by a heavy hit or by chance.'
source_rule (new): 'Code it when the sources say a hit can switch off one function (movement, steering, a weapon) while the unit lives on, however the part is chosen. Being disabled as a whole and burning at low health is critical-burn, not zonal.'
example: 'Battlefield 4: heavy hits cause mobility kills' -> 'Battlefield 4: a heavy hit can knock out a vehicle's movement, or a helicopter's control, for a few seconds'
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: zonal (A, B, C) with nothing left to doubt; the two gaps close. Critical-burn stays separate (A, B, C).
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. The label 'Zonal damage' can stay. On cards, zonal now also covers 'a big hit stalls you'. The excluded sizes (tiny, small) stay.

proposals.evidence: C-coh1 hesitation and unclear rule: 'crew-casualties cites Company of Heroes squads as its example, yet the term bans the squad crew model'. A-coh1: 'crew-casualties is banned for squads'. A-battlefield, B-battlefield and C-battlefield weighed it for the canopy-glass sniper hits, found only in Battlefield 2. All coders left it out.
proposals.root_cause: The term's first example (CoH soldiers and gun crewmen tracked one by one) describes a squad or team weapon, which the term's excluded.crew-models [solo, squad, remote] rules out. The example and the rule contradict each other.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json term crew-casualties: examples[0] removed, new source_rule
proposals.change:
Remove examples[0] 'Company of Heroes: each soldier and gun crewman is tracked; a gun without crew can be captured'. Keep the Foxhole and Wargame examples.
source_rule (new): 'Code it only for a unit with two or more seats whose sources say hits can kill or throw out the people inside while it survives (open seats, shots through the glass). Never for a squad: losing members is part of the squad crew model.'
proposals.expected: Riflemen: no crew-casualties (A, B, C), flat-pool. Attack helicopter: the glass shots are in Battlefield 2 only, which series-titles leaves out, so no crew-casualties (A, B, C as now), and the three-model cap no longer pinches.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. No change to excluded.crew-models. How a CoH team weapon (MG team) is crewed is for the crew group to decide; this rule only bans squads.

proposals.evidence: Riflemen: A-coh1, B-coh1 and C-coh1 all hesitated between flat-pool and evasive ('CoH has an explicit hit-chance system: received accuracy, cover, veterancy harder to hit'). Gaps from all three: 'cover-based protection'; A-coh1 also 'per-member health within a squad'. A-coh1 unclear rule: 'It is unclear whether CoH's explicit hit-chance system qualifies as evasive'. C-coh1 unclear rule on game-wide mechanics (cover, veterancy, retreat). A-ra3 left out the Hammer's heroic-rank self-heal as a veterancy effect. 3 of 3 coh1 reports plus A-ra3.
proposals.root_cause: evasive asks for 'an explicit evasion mechanic (a miss chance)' but does not say whose it must be; CoH has a miss chance, but it comes from position and rank. No rule says that protection from cover, veterancy or orders is not the unit's own armour. self-repair's RA3 example ('top-rank ... vehicles heal themselves') counts a veterancy effect as a model. Nothing says how to code a squad, whose members each have their own health.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json: list description; term evasive new source_rule; term self-repair examples[0]
proposals.change:
List description, append: 'Code what this unit has. Protection that comes from where it stands or what it has earned, such as cover, veterancy ranks, the retreat bonus or difficulty settings, is not a model, even though the unit benefits; mention it in armour.notes. A model built into the unit's own armour counts even when every unit of its kind in the game shares it (Company of Heroes rear armour). For a squad, code what protects each member; losing members is part of the squad crew model.'
evasive source_rule (new): 'Code it only when the unit itself has a way to dodge: a dodge roll, a stated chance to avoid hits, or a hard-to-hit trait of its own. Hit chance from cover, rank or moving, which every soldier of the game gets, is not evasive.'
self-repair: remove examples[0] 'Red Alert 3: top-rank and some heavy vehicles heal themselves' (top-rank healing is veterancy, which the new rule leaves out).
proposals.expected: Riflemen: flat-pool only (A, B, C), with cover, veterancy and retreat in armour.notes, as all three already wrote. The three cover gaps and the per-member gap close. Hammer: heroic self-heal not coded (A's reasoning confirmed; B and C did the same). CoH vehicles still get directional.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Cover stays a map and class matter (the infantry class says it uses cover). Pairs with the abilities group's answer to C-coh1's game-wide question; this rule settles only the armour side. Units in scope: CoH and DoW infantry (cover, veterancy) come out flat-pool unless they have their own model; units with a dodge of their own (a shooter dodge roll, a hard-to-hit commando) keep evasive.

proposals.evidence: A-battlefield ('With a cap of 3, adding one drops another') and C-battlefield ('With a three-model cap, I had to choose which title's mechanics win').
proposals.root_cause: A researched unit may carry up to three models, but nothing says which to keep when more apply.
proposals.target: data/vocab/armour-models.json: list description, the sentence 'A card has one or two; a researched unit up to three.'
proposals.change: 'A card has one or two; a researched unit up to three.' -> 'A card has one or two; a researched unit up to three. If more apply, keep the rarest (rare, then uncommon, then common; on a tie, the one listed first here) and name the others in armour.notes.'
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: with series-titles only three models apply (critical-burn, self-repair, zonal), so nothing changes for A, B, C. If a coder still counted Battlefield 2's crew-casualties, the rule would keep crew-casualties, critical-burn and zonal and drop self-repair, so two coders could not differ.
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Uses the existing rarity field; no validator change. Leans the data toward rarer mechanics, which suits a concept generator.

proposals.evidence: Armour models: A-battlefield, B-battlefield and C-battlefield all weighed crew-casualties, sourced only for Battlefield 2, and zonal, found only in Battlefield 4 ('No rule says which titles of a series entry count'). countered_by: B-battlefield ('the explicit statements come from the BF2 section'). Unclear rules: B-battlefield ('which titles count for a series entry') and C-battlefield ('no rule says which title wins ... or whether to take the union of mechanics'). 3 of 3 battlefield reports.
proposals.root_cause: games.json battlefield.version_researched says Battlefield 3 and 4 lead, with other titles 'for archetypes they add'. Nothing says whether a fact from another title of the same archetype may fill a field, or what to do when the lead titles differ.
proposals.target: scripts/build-docs.mjs Conventions list (new 'Series' bullet, shown in docs/fields.md) and schemas/game.schema.json $defs.game.properties.version_researched description. Cross-group: also governs cooldown and on-death values, so the groups for those fields should agree.
proposals.change:
New Conventions bullet: '**Series.** For a games.json entry of kind series, a mechanic counts when a lead title named in version_researched has it, or a title named there for the archetype being coded. Facts from the series' other titles do not fill fields; mention them in notes. When the lead titles differ, code the mechanic and say in notes which title has it. Matchups follow from the coded parts.'
version_researched description: 'Patch, edition or date the research describes.' -> 'Patch, edition or date the research describes. For a series, name the lead titles and any title used for an archetype it adds; facts from its other titles do not fill fields.'
proposals.expected: Attack helicopter: zonal (Battlefield 4, a lead title) coded by A, B, C. crew-casualties (Battlefield 2 only) left out by A, B, C, with the glass shots in armour.notes, as B already did. countered_by: B's entries stay, because jets with anti-air missiles and tank guns that reach low fliers are coded parts of BF3/4 units; A, B and C already share role:anti-air, weapon:guided-missiles, mobility:jet and weapon:cannon. The BF2 flare recharge no longer sets a cooldown band (abilities group).
proposals.side_effects: Run npm run docs. Applies to battlefield, wargame and mechwarrior, the three series entries. No validator change.

proposals.evidence: Gaps A-sc2, B-sc2 and C-sc2 (all three SC2 reports): 'a negative self-link such as cannot hit low-air or high-air'. The tank's best-known weakness, no anti-air at all, could only be written on the enemy side. Unclear rules A-ra3 ('Weaknesses that are absences ... a lacks or cannot-hit link kind would make these consistent'), B-sc2 and C-sc2. The RA3 sample shows the workaround: the Hammer's weakness weapon:cannon carries the reason 'can't hit aircraft'. Matchups as a whole: hesitations in 9 of 12 reports.
proposals.root_cause: A weakness link must describe a part the unit has (the validator warns otherwise), so a missing ability, the most common RTS weakness, cannot be written. Coders hang it on an unrelated part or move it to countered_by, which hides it from the generator's strength-weakness pairing.

proposals.root_cause: The Typed links convention lists the link kinds but gives no order of choice, no rule for unit links or for links to the unit itself, none for comparators on the unit's own values, none for the air layers in an RTS, none for an enemy that wins or loses depending on tactics, and none for planned-pattern links.

proposals.change: New bullet: '**Matchups.** Write the reason first, then pick the link that names the part behind it. (1) Name the other unit the way the sources do: by its job (role:anti-armour, role:anti-air) when they name a job; by what it fires when they name a weapon (weapon:machine-gun) or a kind of harm (damage:electric); by what it is (class:aircraft, class:infantry, armour-class:heavy) when they name a kind of unit. (2) For fliers, use class:aircraft when the point holds for every flier; use target:low-air or target:high-air only when it holds for one layer. (3) Prefer word-list links. Add a unit: link only for a same-game partner or rival the sources name, next to a word-list link for the same reason. A link to the unit itself is fine in combos when the sources say it works best in numbers. (4) In strengths and weaknesses, give the unit's own value with no <= or >= (range:long, not range:>=long). Use comparators only in counters, countered by and combos, for a group of units. (5) Something the unit lacks is a weakness written with ! (see Typed links). (6) The same enemy may sit in counters and in countered by only when the two reasons name different situations. Otherwise put it where the head-on fight at equal cost ends, and give the tactic that turns it in the reason. (7) Most important first; keep each list short, about two to five. A link to a planned pattern is fine; its warning clears when the pattern is written. (8) A unit: link to a unit not yet researched uses the slug its entry would get: the in-game name, dropping a final Squad or Team (Riflemen Squad -> riflemen).'
proposals.expected: The lists stay open choices; the guidance aims at usefulness, not at forcing agreement. Siege Tank countered_by: A's target:low-air becomes class:aircraft (all three now share it); C's unit:sc2.protoss.immortal and unit:sc2.terran.thor get role:anti-armour next to them, so all three share role:anti-armour; weaknesses gain !hits:low-air for all three. Hammer counters: C's unit links get class:vehicle beside them (shared with A, B and the sample). Terror Drone combos: C's unit:ra3.soviet.bullfrog and twinblade get role:transport (shared with A and the sample). Attack helicopter: B's range:long is the right form; pattern:mark-target in combos (B, C) is accepted without doubt. Riflemen: A's machine-gun entries on both lists stay, because the reasons name different situations (head-on vs grenades); A's slug becomes coh1.wehrmacht.volksgrenadier. Overlap should rise on the shared core (roles, weapons, classes), while extra entries remain each coder's choice.

(1) Name the other unit the way the sources do: by its job (role:anti-armour, role:anti-air) when they name a job; by what it fires when they name a weapon (weapon:machine-gun) or a kind of harm (damage:electric); by what it is (class:aircraft, class:infantry, armour-class:heavy) when they name a kind of unit. When they name only a unit, use the same order for what makes that unit win. (2) For fliers, use class:aircraft when the sources mean air units in general; use target:low-air or target:high-air only when the point holds for one layer. (3) Prefer word-list and pattern links. Add a unit: link only for a same-game partner or rival the sources name, next to a word-list or pattern link for the same reason. A link to the unit itself is fine in combos when the sources say it works best in numbers. (4) In strengths and weaknesses, give the unit's own value with no <= or >= (range:long, not range:>=long; passengers:1, not passengers:>=1). Use comparators only in counters, countered by and combos, for a group of units. (5) Something the unit lacks is written with ! (see Typed links): in weaknesses for its own gap, in counters for enemies with that gap. (6) The same enemy may sit in counters and in countered by only when the two reasons name different situations. Otherwise put it where the head-on fight at equal cost ends, and give the tactic that turns it in the reason. (7) Most important first; keep each list short, about two to five. A link to a planned pattern is fine; its warning clears when the pattern is written. (8) A unit: link to a unit not yet researched uses the slug its entry would get: the in-game name, dropping a final Squad or Team (Riflemen Squad -> riflemen).'
Append 'See Matchups under Conventions.' to the five field descriptions. Docs only; no validator change. Say when merging that item (8) touches the Ids convention.
